description: Topic hierarchy for Business and Economics (Eritrean MoE textbooks Grades 10–12), linking concepts, keywords, textbook pages and exam questions.

topics.title: Basic economic concepts
topics.concept: Economics studies how individuals and societies use scarce resources to satisfy unlimited wants. Scarcity forces choices (what, how, for whom to produce), which are answered differently by free market, command and mixed economic systems.

subtopics.title: Definition of economics, scarcity and choice
subtopics.concept: Economics is the study of how individuals and societies choose to use their scarce resources to satisfy their material wants as much as possible. Resources are limited, wants are unlimited – this scarcity is the basic economic problem.

textbook_refs.section: Unit 1 introduction – Scarcity, choice and the definition of economics

subtopics.title: Production possibilities curve
subtopics.concept: The PPC shows the combinations of two goods an economy can produce with all its resources and technology. Points on the curve are efficient, points inside are attainable but inefficient, points outside are unattainable. Moving along the curve shows opportunity cost.

textbook_refs.section: 1.1.3 Production Possibilities Curve (PPC)

subtopics.title: Factors of production
subtopics.concept: Land (natural resources, reward rent), labour (human effort, wage), capital (man-made goods used to produce other goods, interest) and entrepreneurship (decision making and risk taking, profit).

textbook_refs.section: 1.1.1 Types of Factors of Production
1.1.1 Types of Factors of Production

subtopics.title: Economic systems
subtopics.concept: Free market (capitalist): private property, economic freedom, voluntary exchange, profit motive, competition; prices set by supply and demand. Command: public ownership, central planning. Mixed: features of both.

textbook_refs.section: Unit 1 introduction – (ii) Economic Systems: capitalist/free market system

subtopics.title: Forms of business organization
subtopics.concept: Sole proprietorship, partnership (unlimited liability), corporation (separate legal entity, ownership in shares, limited liability, continuity, large capital, professional employees; disadvantages: double taxation, large initial cost, owner–manager conflict) and cooperatives.

textbook_refs.section: 1.2 Business Organizations – C. Corporation
1.2 Business Organizations – Advantages of corporation

subtopics.title: Transportation and communication
subtopics.concept: Transport: road, railway, water, air, pipeline (liquids and gases such as petroleum), ropeway, human- and animal-powered. Modern communication systems: visual, acoustic (telephone, telegraph, record player), telecommunication and data-processing.

textbook_refs.section: 1.3.2 Communication Systems – Acoustic Communication Systems
1.3.1 Transportation Systems – E. Pipeline transportation

topics.title: Money, banking and insurance
topics.concept: Money replaced barter; it is a medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value and standard of deferred payment. Central banks manage the monetary system; commercial and specialised banks serve the public; insurance transfers risk.

subtopics.title: Barter, functions and forms of money
subtopics.concept: Barter = exchange of goods for goods without money (needs double coincidence of wants). Functions of money: medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value, standard of deferred payments. Metallic money: standard (full-bodied) coins – metal value = face value; token coins – face value > metal value.

textbook_refs.section: 2.1.2 Forms of Money – Metallic money
2.1.1 Functions of Money – iv. Standard of deferred payments
1.1.1 Measuring National Economic Performance – c) National Income
1.4.3 Exchange Rates

subtopics.title: Central bank, commercial banks and banks in Eritrea
subtopics.concept: Central bank: issues currency, banker/agent/adviser to government, holds member banks' reserves, lender of last resort. Commercial banks accept deposits and grant loans. Eritrea: Bank of Eritrea, Commercial Bank, Housing and Commerce Bank, Eritrean Development and Investment Bank, and the Savings and Micro-Credit Program (loans to poor households and small businesses).

textbook_refs.section: 2.2.1 Types of Banks – Functions of a Central Bank (National Bank)
2.2.2 Banks in Eritrea – Savings and Micro-Credit Program (SMCP)

subtopics.title: Insurance – characteristics and legal principles
subtopics.concept: Characteristics: sharing (pooling) of losses, payment of accidental losses, risk transfer (possibility of loss moves from insured to insurer), indemnification. Legal principles: indemnity, insurable interest, subrogation (textbook: an individual should not claim compensation from two sources), utmost good faith, contribution.

textbook_refs.section: 2.3.1 Basic Characteristics of Insurance – c. Risk Transfer
2.3.2 Legal Principles of Insurance – iii. Principle of subrogation

topics.title: Basic microeconomic concepts
topics.concept: Market structures, demand and supply, elasticity, short-run costs and consumer choice (marginal utility and indifference curves).

subtopics.title: Market structures
subtopics.concept: Perfect competition: many buyers/sellers, homogeneous products, perfect information, perfect mobility, free entry/exit, horizontal firm demand curve. Monopoly: one seller, no close substitutes, fixes EITHER price OR quantity, downward-sloping demand. Monopolistic competition, oligopoly, duopoly. Buyer side: monopsony (one buyer), oligopsony (few buyers).

textbook_refs.section: 1.1.1 Market Structure – a) Monopoly
1.1.1 Market Structure – Monopsony and Oligopsony
1.1.1 Market Structure – i) Perfect competition

subtopics.title: Demand, related goods and exceptions
subtopics.concept: Law of demand: price up → quantity demanded down. Exceptions: Giffen and Veblen goods (demand rises with price). Substitutes (sugar–honey) vs complements (car–gasoline). Normal goods: demand rises with income; inferior goods: demand falls as income rises.

subtopics.title: Elasticity of demand
subtopics.concept: Ped = %ΔQd ÷ %ΔP, computed from the ORIGINAL values: [(Q₂ − Q₁)/Q₁] ÷ [(P₂ − P₁)/P₁]; sign usually dropped. Ped > 1 elastic, = 1 unitary, < 1 inelastic, 0 perfectly inelastic, ∞ perfectly elastic. Income elasticity negative for inferior goods.

subtopics.title: Short-run costs of production
subtopics.concept: TC = TFC + TVC. Fixed costs do not change with output and must be paid even at zero output; variable costs change with output. For TC = a + bQ, TFC = a and TVC = bQ.

textbook_refs.section: 1.4 Cost of Production – short-term fixed and variable costs
1.4 Cost of Production – TC = TFC + TVC

subtopics.title: Consumer choice: marginal utility and indifference curves
subtopics.concept: Consumer equilibrium: MUA/PA = MUB/PB. A price fall → buy more → MU falls (diminishing MU), giving a downward-sloping demand curve. Indifference curves slope downward, are convex to the origin, higher curves = more satisfaction, and never intersect.

textbook_refs.section: 1.5 Consumer Choice and Demand – consumer equilibrium and deriving the demand curve

topics.title: Basic macroeconomic concepts
topics.concept: National income accounting, consumption/saving/investment, public finance and international trade.

subtopics.title: National income measures
subtopics.concept: GDP/GNP, NNP = GNP − depreciation, NI = income of factors (wages, rent, interest, profit) / NNP − indirect business taxes, PI, disposable income Yd = PI − personal taxes, personal saving = Yd − C. Expenditure approach C + I + G + (X − M); consumption is the largest component. Per capita income = GDP or GNP ÷ population.

subtopics.title: Consumption, saving and investment
subtopics.concept: C = a + bYd → S = −a + (1 − b)Yd. MPC + MPS = 1. Net investment = gross investment − depreciation. Investment demand depends on the interest rate and the marginal efficiency of capital.

subtopics.title: Public finance
subtopics.concept: Public finance studies how the government raises revenue and makes expenditure. Government intervenes because of public goods, externalities (costs/benefits to third parties) and inequality. Taxation is the major source of public revenue.

subtopics.title: International trade, balance of payments and exchange rates
subtopics.concept: Comparative advantage = lower opportunity cost. Terms of trade = Px/Pm. BOP: current account (goods and services), capital account (investments and loans), official reserve account. Exchange rate = price of one currency in terms of another.

subtopics.title: Accounting equation
subtopics.concept: Assets = Liabilities + Capital. Changes must balance: ΔA = ΔL + ΔC.

subtopics.title: Transaction analysis and debit/credit rules
subtopics.concept: Assets and expenses (and drawings) increase on the debit side; liabilities, capital and revenue increase on the credit side. Buying equipment for cash: Dr Equipment, Cr Cash. Owner's investment: Dr Cash, Cr Capital.

subtopics.title: Journal, ledger, posting and chart of accounts
subtopics.concept: Chart of accounts = list of account titles and numbers showing their arrangement in the ledger. Posting transfers journal amounts to ledger accounts; the journal page number goes in the ledger's Post Ref. column and the account number in the journal's Post Ref. column (last step). Account balance = difference between the two sides.

subtopics.title: Trial balance, errors, fiscal period and worksheet
subtopics.concept: The trial balance proves equality of debits and credits but does not detect errors such as an equal wrong amount on both sides, omitted or duplicated transactions, or posting to a wrong account of the same type. Fiscal (accounting) period = length of time covered by the analysis.

topics.unit: Unit 2 – Bookkeeping for a Merchandising Business
topics.concept: Special journals (purchase, cash payments, sales, cash receipts), the general journal, subsidiary ledgers, the ten-column worksheet, adjusting and closing entries.

subtopics.title: Special journals, discounts and posting
subtopics.concept: Purchase journal: merchandise bought on account (total: Dr Purchases, Cr A/P). Sales journal: merchandise sold on account (total: Dr A/R, Cr Sales). Cash payments journal: every cash payment (purchase discount column). Cash receipts journal: every cash receipt (sales discount column). General journal: adjusting, closing, reversing entries, returns and allowances, other assets on account. 2/10, n/30: 2% discount if paid within 10 days.

subtopics.concept: Ten-column worksheet: unadjusted TB, adjustments, adjusted TB, income statement, balance sheet. Typical adjustments: merchandise inventory, supplies, prepaid insurance, prepaid rent, depreciation. Goods available for sale = beginning inventory + purchases; COGS = available − ending inventory. Credit-balance temporary accounts (revenue, purchases discount, purchases returns) and debit-balance ones are closed to Income Summary.

topics.unit: Unit 2 – Control of Cash, the Payroll and Payroll Records, and Plant Assets
topics.concept: Internal control of cash, petty cash, cheques and bank reconciliation; payroll (Eritrean income tax, overtime, payroll records); plant assets and depreciation.

subtopics.title: Internal control of cash, cheques and petty cash
subtopics.concept: Cash is the most liquid asset. Receipts control: deposit all receipts daily, verify sales, separate duties. Disbursement control: establishment of responsibility, segregation of duties, documentation, physical controls, independent verification, vouchers. Drawer signs a cheque, drawee (bank) pays, payee receives. Petty cash (imprest): Dr Petty Cash only when established or increased; replenish by Dr expenses, Cr Cash.

subtopics.title: Plant assets and depreciation
subtopics.concept: Tangible assets have physical substance; intangible do not (patents, goodwill). Useful life is limited by physical deterioration and obsolescence. Straight-line depreciation = (cost − residual value) ÷ useful life. Book value = cost − accumulated depreciation; plant assets are shown on the balance sheet at book value.
